findings.finding: Valid legacy Git history adoption is rejected: require_sha256 requires 64 lowercase hex characters but provenance SHA_RE requires exactly 40 for legacy_history_tip (target_provenance.py:33,4427). No tip satisfies both contracts. Real approved commit-subject/v2 adoption cannot pass apply and finalization.
findings.remediation: Validate the Git commit identifier with the canonical Git SHA contract; retain SHA-256 for incoming_policy_sha256. Exercise an approved reachable legacy tip through the runner.

findings.finding: AC3 lacks origin-specific semantic evidence. All origins are initialized by the incoming initializer with an empty ledger; customized mode changes only a retired alias (lines151-156). Candidate ledger remains empty and effective state is freshly reduced to one evidence rule/review route (lines106-111,221-226,260). Hash checks do not establish preservation/reconciliation of an existing customized capability/rule/contract, provider/component cutovers, or Git grammar adoption. The runner therefore bypasses the very adoption path affected by R1.
findings.remediation: Add bounded origin-specific fixtures and assertions for the required semantic cutovers, including a nonempty target-owned semantic customization disposition and explicit legacy grammar adoption. Keep decisions fixture-owned and record preserved/replaced/retired outcomes.

findings.finding: AC4 negative evidence is incomplete. The target cases reject only missing approval and missing validation receipt. No case attempts tampered identity/candidate/receipt, ambiguous authority, actual failing target-validator disagreement, or unresolved customization, although AC4 explicitly requires those failures plus unchanged mutation/provenance boundaries. Archive identity checks on valid inputs do not execute these negative cases.
findings.remediation: Add bounded negative cases for the explicit AC4 conditions, assert the intended error reason and exact protected prestate/provenance boundaries; retain failures distinctly.

limitations: No matrix, tests, transport or provider execution performed. Recovery structure inspected only; no dynamic pass claimed.
Source-only package inclusion is an independently identified parent finding and reported first execution failure; this audit does not duplicate it or claim a package pass.
Current-schema fixture seeding is not intrinsically prohibited; its limited semantics cannot by itself satisfy the broader AC3.
No tracked files changed; root owns repairs and integration.
